In a single day, a company that didn't exist six years ago became worth more on the stock market than Meta.
On Thursday, November 19, Anthropic, the company behind the Claude assistant, listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker A-N-T.
The IPO price had been set the night before at 83 dollars, above the expected range of 70 to 78.
At the open, 11:48 New York time, the stock jumped to 111 dollars 50: up 34 percent.
Then the session cooled.
It closed at 97 dollars 17, up 17 percent from the IPO price.
More than 846 million shares changed hands, more than SpaceX on its first day in June.
According to Forbes, the offering raised 81 billion dollars.
Bloomberg calls it a record IPO.
The valuation depends on how you count: 1.27 trillion dollars on shares outstanding; close to 1.77 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
Either way, that is more than Meta, valued at 1.55 trillion.
The timing is no accident.
For three weeks, the AI sector has been shaken: Nvidia's stock has lost about 20 percent and its CEO, Jensen Huang, has resigned.
Investors were asking whether the AI bubble was about to deflate.
Anthropic chose this moment to test their appetite.
The result: a strong start, but a close 13 percent below the day's high.
Scenario one: confidence returns.
The stock settles above its IPO price and lifts chip suppliers across Asia.
Scenario two: volatility continues.
Retail investors, very active on day one, take their profits.
Scenario three: the domino effect.
Other AI players speed up their own listings to catch the window.
One thing is certain: for the first time, a pure AI company is publicly traded.
Every trading day is now a real-time poll on the future of artificial intelligence.
